destinations.name: Cox's Bazar
destinations.description: Stretching 120 kilometres along the Bay of Bengal, Cox's Bazar is Bangladesh's crown jewel of the coast. Golden sands, rolling waves, fresh seafood, and a lively boardwalk make it the country's most beloved escape. Watch the sunset paint the horizon over Himchari, ride a motorbike along Marine Drive, and end the day with grilled pomfret by the shore.
destinations.best_time_to_visit: November to March — cool, dry, and perfect beach weather
destinations.weather_notes: Tropical monsoon; humid summers, mild winters, rainy June–September
popular_attractions: Inani Beach — miles of golden sand and coral pebbles
Himchari National Park & waterfall viewpoint
Marine Drive — a 40km oceanfront scenic road
Laboni Beach boardwalk and night market
Ramu Buddhist temples and craft villages
Cox's Bazar Lighthouse viewpoint
destinations.recommended_accommodation: Beachfront resorts in Kolatoli, boutique guest houses near Sugandha Point, and budget stays along Laboni Road. Ocean-view rooms book out fast in December–January.
destinations.travel_tips:
Book beachfront hotels 2–4 weeks ahead in peak season
Carry light cotton clothing and reef-safe sunscreen
Try the fresh tiger prawns and churpi from local stalls
Use the Marine Drive route early morning to beat the sun
Keep a power bank — long beach walks drain phones fast
destinations.seo_description: The world's longest natural sea beach

gallery.caption: Sunset over the Bay of Bengal

destinations.name: Saint Martin's Island
destinations.description: Bangladesh's only coral island is a tiny teardrop of white sand and clear, turquoise water sitting at the southernmost point of the country. Coconut palms, fishing boats, and a slow island rhythm define Narikel Jinjira — the island of coconuts. Snorkel among coral reefs, eat crab curry on the beach, and fall asleep to the sound of the tide.
destinations.best_time_to_visit: November to February — calm seas, clear visibility for snorkelling
destinations.weather_notes: Tropical island climate; the island is closed to visitors during monsoon storms
popular_attractions: Narikel Jinjira beach — the island's iconic sandbar
Snorkelling and coral reef spotting at the south point
Chhera Dwip — a separate islet reachable by foot at low tide
Fishermen's village and boat-building traditions
Sunset boat rides around the island
destinations.recommended_accommodation: Simple beach cottages and small resorts in the northern and middle parts of the island. Electricity is limited at night; generators and solar power are common.
destinations.travel_tips:
Access is by launch or speedboat from Teknaf (approx. 2–3 hours)
Island is reachable only in season — verify the ferry schedule
Carry cash; ATMs are unavailable on the island
Reef-safe sunscreen only — the coral ecosystem is fragile
Pack a torch for the island's limited night lighting
destinations.seo_title: Saint Martin's Island Travel Guide | Atithi
destinations.seo_description: The turquoise gem of the Bay of Bengal

destinations.name: The Sundarbans
destinations.description: The largest mangrove forest on Earth and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the Sundarbans is a haunting maze of tidal rivers, mudflats, and dense mangrove. Home to the Royal Bengal Tiger, saltwater crocodiles, and the endangered Irrawaddy dolphin, it is Bangladesh's wildest frontier. Glide through silent creeks at dawn, watch deer and monkeys on the banks, and feel the pulse of a forest that has no equals.
destinations.best_time_to_visit: November to February — cool, dry weather and better wildlife sightings
destinations.weather_notes: Humid and tropical; heavy rain June–October, strong tides year-round
popular_attractions: Kotka & Kachikhali wildlife viewpoints
Tiger Point — best chance of pugmark and tiger sightings
Dublar Char — the fisherman island and sea-beach
Hiron Point — dolphin and crocodile spotting
Karambol forest watchtower
Traditional Mawali honey-collecting villages
destinations.recommended_accommodation: Tours typically stay aboard comfortable river cruise vessels with cabins, meals, and guides. Some forest camps offer basic eco-lodging at Kotka and Karambol.
destinations.travel_tips:
A forest permit is required and is arranged by your tour operator
Take an experienced guide — navigation is genuinely challenging
Book a multi-day cruise (2 nights+) to reach the deep forest
Bring insect repellent and long sleeves for evenings
Binoculars are essential for wildlife viewing
destinations.seo_description: The mangrove kingdom of the Royal Bengal Tiger

destinations.name: Sylhet
destinations.description: Northeastern Bangladesh is a landscape of emerald tea gardens rolling into hazy hills. Sylhet's lush greenery, cool climate, and the famous water-meets-sky canals of Ratargul Swamp Forest make it a completely different Bangladesh. Chase the Jaflong river with its floating stone-laden boats, stand under the thunder of waterfalls, and sip fresh tea straight from the estate.
destinations.best_time_to_visit: October to April — the greenery is lush and the hills are dry enough to hike
destinations.weather_notes: Subtropical; Sylhet is one of Bangladesh's wettest regions, so pack for sudden rain
popular_attractions: Ratargul Swamp Forest — boat rides through submerged trees
Jaflong — river, hills, and floating stone collection
Srimangal tea estates and tea-tasting sessions
Lalakhal — jade-green river surrounded by hills
Bichanakandi — a river confluence framed by tea gardens
Lawachara National Park for gibbon spotting
destinations.recommended_accommodation: Heritage tea-bungalow stays, boutique eco-resorts near Srimangal, and comfortable hotels in Sylhet city. The tea estate bungalows are a highlight experience.
destinations.travel_tips:
Srimangal is the best base for tea-country day trips
Hire a local guide for Lawachara — trails are poorly marked
Best photos of the tea gardens are early morning or late afternoon
The wet season can wash out Jaflong roads — check conditions
destinations.seo_description: Tea gardens, waterfalls and rolling green hills

gallery.caption: Striped tea gardens at golden hour

destinations.name: Bandarban
destinations.description: Bandarban is where Bangladesh gets vertical. Home to Tajingdong — the country's highest peak — and the misty heights of Nilgiri, this hill district rewards travelers with layered mountain views that feel a world away from the plains. Trek through tribal villages, cross suspension bridges over emerald rivers, and sleep above the clouds.
destinations.best_time_to_visit: November to March — clear skies and cool mountain air
destinations.weather_notes: Cool and misty in the hills; rain is heavy during monsoon (June–September)
popular_attractions: Nilgiri — panoramic viewpoints at 2,100ft
Boga Lake — a hidden lake cradled by peaks
Nafakhum & Amiakhum waterfalls in Remakri
Chimbuk hill and the tribal Mro villages
Thanchi bazaar and the stunning road along the Sangu river
Meghla tourist complex and the hanging bridge
destinations.recommended_accommodation: Hilltop resorts at Nilgiri, basic guest houses in Bandarban town, and eco-cabins for trekkers heading to Boga Lake. Book Nilgiri in advance for sunrise views.
destinations.travel_tips:
Hill district permits are needed for non-residents — your operator handles this
Trekking requires reasonable fitness; distances look short on maps only
Carry layers — evenings at altitude get genuinely cold
Avoid monsoon trekking; trails become dangerous
Hire a local guide for Boga Lake and beyond — it is mandatory in some areas
destinations.seo_description: Clouds, cliffs and the highest peak of Bangladesh

destinations.name: Rangamati
destinations.description: Set along the vast Kaptai Lake, Rangamati is the largest district of Bangladesh and the heart of the Chakma people. The lake — a drowned valley turned inland sea — stretches endlessly between green hills. Cruise between floating markets, visit the Hanging Bridge over the water, and explore the crafts and culture of the indigenous communities.
destinations.best_time_to_visit: October to March — calm lake water and pleasant hills
destinations.weather_notes: Subtropical highlands; cooler than the plains with distinct wet season
popular_attractions: Kaptai Lake cruises between forested islands
Hanging Bridge (Jhulonto Bridge) over the lake
Buddha Dhatu Jadi — the golden pagoda
Chakma King's Palace and tribal museum
Floating markets and lake-side bazaars
Shuvolong waterfall reachable by boat
destinations.recommended_accommodation: Lake-facing resort cottages and tribal-style bungalows on the shore. Staying on the lake edge at sunrise is the memory people keep.
destinations.travel_tips:
A boat tour is the single best way to see Rangamati
Visit the museum early to avoid tour groups
Respect local customs when visiting tribal villages
Carry small notes for handicraft purchases at villages
destinations.seo_description: The lake city of the hills

destinations.name: Sajek Valley
destinations.description: Perched high in the folds of the Tripura hills, Sajek Valley has become the most loved mountain escape in Bangladesh. When the weather turns, a sea of clouds rolls through the valley floor and the hills turn into islands. Panoramic viewpoints, winding mountain roads, and the simple wooden cottages of the Kuki villages make Sajek feel suspended above everything.
destinations.best_time_to_visit: November to March — cloud-sea season with crisp mountain air
destinations.weather_notes: Mountain climate; often foggy and cool, rainy in monsoon
popular_attractions: Konglak Hill viewpoint — the classic Sajek panorama
Malampara viewpoint for sunrise
Kuki and Marma tribal villages
The winding Vangtlang mountain road itself
Stargazing on clear nights — Sajek has little light pollution
destinations.recommended_accommodation: Wooden and bamboo cottages with balconies facing the valley, plus a few more polished hilltop resorts. Wake up inside the clouds and watch them clear.
destinations.travel_tips:
The 2-hour jeep ride up from Dighinala is bumpy — pack light
Go early in the season for reliable cloud-sea mornings
Sunrise (6–7am) is the golden window for photography
Carry warm clothing; Sajek nights can drop to single digits
destinations.seo_description: The cloud-sea kingdom above the world

gallery.caption: A sea of clouds below the ridge

destinations.name: Kuakata
destinations.description: Known as Sagar Kannya — the daughter of the sea — Kuakata is one of the only beaches in the world where you can watch both sunrise and sunset over the water. Its wide, dark-golden beach and the gentle Bay of Bengal make it a quieter, more soulful alternative to Cox's Bazar, ringed by Buddhist temples and the fishing traditions of the Rakhine people.
destinations.best_time_to_visit: October to March — calm sea and the full sunrise/sunset experience
destinations.weather_notes: Tropical coastal; monsoon (June–September) brings heavy surf
popular_attractions: Sunrise and sunset views from the eastern and western points
Fatrar Char — a scenic sandbar at the beach's east end
The 100-year-old Rakhine Buddhist temples (Misripara)
Rakhine fishing village and craft markets
Gangamati reserve forest near the coast
destinations.recommended_accommodation: Beach-facing hotels and cottages in Kuakata town. The quieter eastern side near Fatrar Char is best for a peaceful stay.
destinations.travel_tips:
Kuakata's beauty is wide, flat, and atmospheric — bring a good lens
Rent a bicycle or van to explore the long beach
Respect the fishing communities' evening rituals
Best visited midweek to avoid the weekend crowds
destinations.seo_description: Where the sun rises and sets in the sea

gallery.caption: Both sunrises and sunsets over the bay

destinations.name: Srimangal
destinations.description: Billed as the 'land of two leaves and a bud', Srimangal is the heart of Bangladesh's tea country. Endless carpets of tea stretch toward low forested hills, and the whole town smells faintly of fresh leaves and rain. Walk the estates, taste seven-layer tea, spot gibbons in Lawachara, and cycle between villages that have grown tea for over a century.
destinations.best_time_to_visit: November to April — lush green and comfortable for cycling
destinations.weather_notes: Cool mornings, warm days; monsoon turns the estate roads to mud
popular_attractions: Tea estate walks and guided factory visits
Seven-layer tea tasting at the famous Nilkantha tea cabin
Lawachara National Park — gibbons, lemurs, and rainforest trails
Madhabpur Lake and the surrounding gardens
Bicycle tours through the tea country
Baikka Beel wetland sanctuary for birdwatching
destinations.recommended_accommodation: Charming heritage bungalows converted from colonial-era tea manager houses, plus boutique eco-resorts in the estates. These are among the most characterful stays in Bangladesh.
destinations.travel_tips:
Book a heritage tea bungalow for the full experience
Cycle early morning before the heat — the roads are gorgeous
Guided tea tours are worth the fee; you'll taste the difference
Lawachara is best visited with a local naturalist guide

gallery.caption: Rolling tea estates in green light

destinations.name: Sonargaon & Panam City
destinations.description: Once the capital of the Bengal Sultanate and a fabled trading port, Sonargaon is a walk through a vanished golden age. The eerie, elegant ruins of Panam City — a row of decaying merchant mansions — are among the most photographed places in Bangladesh. Nearby, the Folk Arts and Crafts Museum preserves the textiles, boats, and traditions of the old riverside culture.
destinations.best_time_to_visit: November to March — pleasant weather for long walks through the ruins
destinations.weather_notes: Subtropical; the site is exposed, so mornings and evenings are best
popular_attractions: Panam City — the abandoned merchant quarter
Sonargaon Folk Arts and Crafts Museum
The tomb of Panch Pir and medieval Sultanate mosques
Traditional jamdani weaving villages
Boat-building communities along the riverbank
destinations.recommended_accommodation: Best explored as a day trip from Dhaka. A few heritage resorts near the river offer overnight stays if you want the ruins to yourself.
destinations.travel_tips:
Go on a weekday to avoid large school groups
The museum is small — allow an hour and you'll see it all
Combine with a trip to the nearby Jamdani weaving villages
Hire a guide to bring the Panam City mansions to life
destinations.seo_title: Sonargaon & Panam City Travel Guide | Atithi
destinations.seo_description: The abandoned capital of medieval Bengal

gallery.caption: The crumbling facades of Panam City

destinations.name: Paharpur & Mahasthangarh
destinations.description: Northern Bangladesh holds some of South Asia's most significant archaeological sites. Somapura Mahavihara at Paharpur is the largest Buddhist monastery south of the Himalayas and a UNESCO World Heritage Site — a vast, haunting red-brick courtyard from the 8th century. Mahasthangarh is Bangladesh's oldest known city, a fortified citadel dating back over two millennia.
destinations.best_time_to_visit: October to March — comfortable for exploring open archaeological sites
destinations.weather_notes: Hot and dry in summer; the red-brick ruins need shade and morning visits
popular_attractions: Somapura Mahavihara — the great monastery of Paharpur
The Paharpur museum and excavated stupas
Mahasthangarh — the 2,000-year-old citadel of Bogra
Gokul Medh and other ruins of Mahasthangarh
The museums and terracotta collections of both sites
destinations.recommended_accommodation: Explored as an overnight circuit from Dhaka. Comfortable town hotels in Bogra and Joypurhat are the practical base.
destinations.travel_tips:
The full circuit needs two days — Paharpur then Mahasthangarh
Visit Paharpur at opening time to feel the site in silence
Combine with the Bogra mango and sweets market in summer
A guide adds real depth to the archaeology here
destinations.seo_description: The ancient Buddhist monasteries of the north

destinations.name: Dhaka & Heritage
destinations.description: Chaotic, vibrant, and utterly alive, Old Dhaka is a sensory overload of rickshaws, Mughal-era mansions, spice markets, and riverfront ferries. But the capital is also home to the striking National Parliament by Louis Kahn, serene river fortresses, and the world's finest jamdani weaving. A guided walk turns the chaos into one of Asia's most memorable urban experiences.
destinations.best_time_to_visit: November to February — the mild, dry season is kindest to city walks
destinations.weather_notes: Hot and humid for most of the year; monsoon rains June–September
popular_attractions: Old Dhaka's Lalbagh Fort and Mughal-era mosques
Sadarghat river port — the great launch terminal
Shankhari Bazaar and the Hindu heritage lane
National Parliament (Louis Kahn masterpiece)
Jamdani weaving in the Dhaka suburbs
The Dhaka rickshaw — a declared UNESCO Intangible Heritage
destinations.recommended_accommodation: Everything from heritage hotels in Gulshan to guest houses near Old Dhaka. For heritage walks, staying near Old Dhaka or the riverfront is best.
destinations.travel_tips:
Use an experienced guide — crossing Old Dhaka alone is overwhelming
Start at 7am to see the markets before the heat peaks
Rickshaw rides are a must — negotiate the fare first
A sunset Buriganga river cruise is the perfect finale
destinations.seo_description: The beating heart of the nation

gallery.caption: The city of rickshaws and rivers

tours.title: Cox's Bazar Classic — 3D/2N
tours.short_description: The definitive Cox's Bazar itinerary — 120km of beach, Marine Drive sunsets, and fresh seafood dinners by the Bay of Bengal.
tours.full_description: Spend three unhurried days along the longest natural sea beach in the world. Walk golden sand at dawn, drive the stunning Marine Drive to Himchari, and unwind at Kolatoli beachfront hotels each evening. This is the classic escape, refined: small group, local hosts, and zero hidden costs.
inclusions: Return AC bus/coaster transport from Dhaka
Daily breakfast and two seafood dinners
exclusions: Personal shopping and activities (parasailing, jet ski)

itinerary.description: A morning drive along Marine Drive to Himchari National Park and waterfall viewpoint. Afternoon at Inani Beach — golden sand, coral pebbles, and swimming.

itinerary.title: Return to Dhaka

gallery.caption: Sunset over the Bay of Bengal

faqs.question: Can I book with an advance and pay the rest on tour day?
faqs.answer: Yes. Book with a 40% advance to confirm your seat; the remaining balance is settled on the day of the tour by QR scan or online payment.

faqs.question: Is the beach hotel close to the water?
faqs.answer: Our Kolatoli hotel is within a 2–3 minute walk of Laboni Beach.

tours.title: Cox's Bazar + Saint Martin's Combo — 5D/4N
tours.short_description: The best of the Bay — the world's longest beach plus the turquoise coral island of Saint Martin's, in one seamless itinerary.
tours.full_description: Combine Bangladesh's two most-loved coastlines. Four nights split between the sands of Cox's Bazar and the coral idyll of Saint Martin's Island, with a speedboat crossing, island time on white sand, and fresh seafood every evening. The complete southern escape.
inclusions: Return AC transport Dhaka ↔ Cox's Bazar
2 nights beachfront Cox's Bazar + 2 nights island cottage
Local host for the full trip

tours.full_description: Designed for two. A private ocean-view suite, a couple's dinner by the shore, and unhurried days on the sand with your own dedicated host arranging everything. Special touches from arrival flowers to a sunset boat ride for two.

itinerary.title: Sunset Marine Drive

itinerary.title: Island Day Trip

itinerary.title: Return Home

faqs.question: Can we add a Saint Martin's extension?

itinerary.title: Return to Dhaka
itinerary.description: Morning launch to Teknaf and transport back to Dhaka.

tours.title: Sundarbans Cruise — 3D/2N
tours.short_description: Two nights aboard a comfortable cruise vessel through the mangrove kingdom — tiger country, dolphin channels, and forest silence.
tours.full_description: Sail the tidal rivers of the world's largest mangrove forest on a comfortable cabin vessel. Explore forest watchtowers, spot deer and crocodiles from the deck, and glide into silent creeks where the Royal Bengal Tiger still walks. Includes forest permits, a naturalist guide, and full board.

itinerary.title: Dublar Char → Khulna
itinerary.description: Morning visit to Dublar Char fishing island, then sail back to Khulna to complete the journey.

faqs.question: Will we see a tiger?
faqs.answer: Tiger sightings are rare, but you will see pugmarks, deer, crocodiles, and dolphins. The forest itself is the main event.

tours.title: Sundarbans Express — 2D/1N
tours.short_description: A fast, deep-cut weekend taste of the mangroves for those short on days but long on curiosity.
tours.full_description: The essential Sundarbans in 48 hours. A night aboard the vessel, a dawn watchtower visit, and a cruise past the wildlife channels of the outer forest. Designed for busy travelers who want the experience, not just the postcard.

tours.title: Sylhet Tea Country — 3D/2N
tours.short_description: Tea gardens, misty hills, and a swamp forest — the green heart of northeastern Bangladesh.
tours.full_description: Three days in the emerald northeast. Walk endless tea estates near Srimangal, boat through the drowned trees of Ratargul Swamp Forest, and stand where the Jaflong river pours down from the hills. A gentle, beautiful, deeply green itinerary.

itinerary.title: Tea Estates & Return
itinerary.description: Tea tasting and a final estate drive before returning to Dhaka.

tours.title: Sylhet & Ratargul — 2D/1N
tours.short_description: A swift weekend into the swamp forest and the tea hills — the greenest 48 hours in Bangladesh.

itinerary.title: Bichanakandi & Return

tours.short_description: Nilgiri viewpoints, tribal villages, and the road above the clouds — a compact highland escape.
tours.full_description: Head for the highest horizons in Bangladesh. From the sweeping views at Nilgiri to the hanging bridge at Meghla and a cruise along the Sangu river, this is the classic Bandarban highlands in a tight, well-paced two days.

itinerary.description: Drive to Bandarban, afternoon at Meghla and the hanging bridge, sunset at Chimbuk.

itinerary.title: Nilgiri & Sangu River
itinerary.description: Dawn at Nilgiri viewpoint, a Sangu river boat ride, then return to Dhaka.

faqs.question: Do we need hill tract permits?
faqs.answer: Yes — for non-residents of the Chittagong Hill Tracts. We arrange all permits for you as part of the package.

tours.title: Boga Lake Trekking — 3D/2N
tours.short_description: Trek to the hidden lake cradled by Bangladesh's highest peaks, with a night above the clouds.
tours.full_description: A proper mountain trek to Boga Lake — a jade-green lake at 1,200ft surrounded by forested peaks. Camp or stay in a tribal eco-cabin, wake to fog lifting off the water, and trek back through the hill villages. Fitness required, reward guaranteed.

gallery.caption: Boga Lake in the morning mist

tours.title: Rangamati Lake Retreat — 2D/1N
tours.short_description: Kaptai Lake, the hanging bridge, and a cruise between forested islands — the lake city in a weekend.
tours.full_description: Two days along the vast Kaptai Lake. Cruise past islands, cross the Jhulonto Bridge, visit the golden Buddha Dhatu Jadi, and stay in a lake-facing cottage to watch the water change colour at dusk.

itinerary.title: Buddha Dhatu Jadi & Return

tours.title: Sajek Valley — 3D/2N
tours.short_description: Two nights above the cloud sea — hilltop cottages, sunrise viewpoints, and the winding road to the kingdom of clouds.
tours.full_description: The complete Sajek experience. Two nights in a hillside cottage above the valley, sunrise from Konglak hill, visits to the Kuki tribal villages, and the unforgettable jeep climb up the mountain road. Go early in the season for the famous cloud sea.

faqs.question: Is the jeep ride comfortable?

tours.title: Sajek Weekend Getaway — 2D/1N

blogPosts.title: Chasing the Sajek Cloud Sea: A Field Guide
blogPosts.excerpt: The cloud sea over Sajek Valley is one of Bangladesh's most magical sights. Here's exactly when to go, where to stand, and what to pack to catch it.
blogPosts.body:
There is a moment in Sajek Valley, just after dawn, when the fog banks lying in the valley floor begin to roll like ocean swell — and the hills turn into islands. It lasts, if you're lucky, for about forty minutes. Then the sun burns through and the whole kingdom of clouds dissolves into an ordinary, beautiful green valley.

That forty minutes is why people drive nine hours. Here is how to make sure you catch it.

### When to go

The cloud sea is a cold-weather phenomenon. Your window is roughly mid-November to early March, when the cold air from the north settles into the valley overnight and condenses into a proper sea of cloud by dawn. December and January are the most reliable months.

Check the weather forecast the night before. A clear, calm, cold night almost guarantees cloud in the morning. A windy or rainy night usually means fog that burns off before sunrise.

### Where to stand

Konglak Hill is the classic viewpoint, but the real secret is the walk along the ridge east of the village — the unmarked trail that locals use. You get the same sea, a wider angle, and none of the crowd. Ask your host to point you to the ridge walk before dawn.

Malampara viewpoint is the second-best option, and it's marginally less crowded than Konglak.

### What to pack

Temperatures at dawn can drop into single digits. A thermal layer, a decent fleece, and a warm hat are not optional in December. A thermos of hot tea will make you the most popular person on the viewpoint.

For photography, bring a lens that can handle low light. The cloud sea is often photographed into the sun, so a small amount of lens flare is part of the look — embrace it.

blogPosts.title: The Sundarbans: Budget Cruise vs. Private Charter
blogPosts.excerpt: Two very different ways to see the mangrove kingdom. Which one is right for you, your group, and your tolerance for shared bathrooms.
blogPosts.body:
There are two Sundarbans experiences, and they share almost nothing except the forest. The first is the group cruise — twelve to twenty travelers on a comfortable vessel, shared cabins, a fixed route, and a per-head price that keeps the adventure affordable. The second is the private charter — your group, your itinerary, your schedule, and the freedom to linger where the wildlife is.

### The budget cruise

Group cruises are the smart way to see the Sundarbans on a realistic budget. You get a cabin, three meals a day, a naturalist guide, and the full Kotka–Karambol–Dublar Char circuit for a fraction of the charter price. The trade-offs are real: shared cabins mean less privacy, the fixed route means you move on even if a tiger was just spotted, and the boat stops where the group wants it to.

### The private charter

A private charter costs two to three times more per person, but for wildlife photographers and serious nature travellers it is usually worth every taka. You control the speed, you can sit in a channel for an extra hour watching dolphins, and you get a proper cabin with private facilities.

### Which one to book

If you're a first-timer who just wants to see the mangrove kingdom safely and affordably, book the group cruise and bring a good pair of binoculars. If you're a photographer, a family travelling together, or a group of six or more, the charter — split six ways — is surprisingly reasonable.

blogPosts.title: Tasting the Bengal Food Trail: 8 Dishes to Try
blogPosts.excerpt: From Sylhet's seven-layer tea to Kuakata's crab curry, a traveller's guide to the dishes that define each region of Bangladesh.
blogPosts.body:
Travel in Bangladesh is often described in terms of sights — beaches, hills, ruins. But ask any Bangladeshi about a trip and they'll recount the meals first. Food is the connective tissue of every journey here, and each region has a signature.

### From the sea

At Cox's Bazar, the move is grilled pomfret at a Laboni beach stall at sunset. In Kuakata, it's crab curry — fiery, sweet, and best eaten with rice and your hands. On Saint Martin's island, the crab dishes get even better because the day's catch never travels further than a boat's length.

### From the hills

In the hill districts, look for bamboo chicken — chicken stuffed into a bamboo tube with herbs and roasted over open flame. In Sylhet, the ritual is seven-layer tea at Nilkantha cabin, each layer a different density of sweetened tea. And in Srimangal, every estate has its own single-origin brew worth tasting side by side.

### From the cities

No food trail through Bangladesh is complete without Dhaka's kacchi biryani — the city's legendary slow-cooked lamb and rice dish. And in the north, around Bogra, the mango season turns the whole town into an open-air fruit market.

blogPosts.title: One Night Above Boga Lake: A Trek Diary
blogPosts.excerpt: Our trekking guide on what it's actually like to sleep beside a jade lake at 1,200 feet in the Chittagong Hill Tracts.
blogPosts.body:
The road to Thanchi ends at the Sangu river, and the real journey begins. From the guest house, the trail climbs through tribal villages, bamboo groves, and afternoon drizzle, until the forest opens and Boga Lake sits below you like a green coin dropped into the hills.

### The climb

The trek is four to six hours depending on your pace, and it is genuinely a climb — switchbacks, loose stone, and a final scramble that tests your knees. Local guides and porters make it straightforward, but anyone who tells you it's a casual walk has not done it with a full backpack.

### The night

The eco-cabins by the lake are basic — a bed, a blanket, a lantern — but the trade is extraordinary. At dusk the lake turns silver, then the sky loads up with stars, and at dawn the mist lifts off the water in ribbons. People plan this trek for the views; they remember it for the silence.

### The descent

Going down is harder on the knees but faster, and you'll pass the same villages in daylight, seeing the vegetable terraces and schoolchildren you missed on the way up. Bring trekking poles if you have them. And if a local porter offers to carry your bag, take the offer — it's a livelihood, not an inconvenience.
